**Sikhae (시계) – Korean Traditional Rice Cake** Sikhae is a simple, comforting dish made from steamed rice flour mixed with water and sweetened with sugar or honey. It’s often served as a snack or dessert, especially during festivals or family gatherings. Below is a straightforward recipe you can try at home. --- ### Ingredients | Ingredient | Amount | Notes | |------------|--------|-------| | Glutinous rice flour (찹쌀가루) | 1 cup (≈120 g) | Use fine‑ground glutinous rice flour for smooth texture. | | Water | 1 ½ cups (≈360 ml) | Adjust slightly for consistency. | | Sugar (white or brown) | ¼–⅓ cup (≈50–70 g) | Sweetness level can be adjusted to taste. | | Optional flavorings | | • Honey or maple syrup (for natural sweetness)
• Vanilla extract (1 tsp)
• Cinnamon or nutmeg (pinch)
• Fruit puree (e.g., strawberry, mango) for fruity variations | | Optional toppings | | • Toasted sesame seeds
• Chopped nuts (almonds, walnuts)
• Fresh fruit slices | --- ### Equipment - Steamer or pot with steaming rack - Mixing bowl - Whisk or spoon - Heat‑resistant container or mold (optional) --- ### Instructions #### 1. Prepare the Steamer Fill a pot with about 2 cm of water and bring it to a gentle boil. Place a steamer rack or a heat‑resistant plate inside. If you don’t have a dedicated steamer, you can use a colander or a metal sieve that fits over the pot. #### 2. Mix the Dough In a mixing bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour and sugar. Gradually add the water while whisking continuously to avoid lumps. The batter should be thick but pourable—similar to a thick pancake batter. If you’re adding vanilla or spices, stir them in now. #### 3. Steam the Sikhae Pour the batter into a heat‑resistant container or spread it thinly onto a parchment‑lined tray if you prefer flat cakes. Cover the container or tray loosely with foil or a lid to keep steam trapped. Steam for **15–20 minutes**, or until the surface turns translucent and the interior is cooked through. Check by inserting a toothpick; it should come out clean. #### 4. Cool & Slice Remove the container from the steamer and let it cool for a few minutes. Once it’s safe to handle, transfer the cake onto a cutting board. Slice into bite‑size pieces or cut into squares/rectangles using a sharp knife. #### 5. Serve & Garnish Serve the sikhae warm or at room temperature. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds or chopped nuts on top for added crunch. You can also drizzle honey or a light syrup over the slices for extra sweetness. For a fruity twist, serve alongside fresh fruit or a fruit puree. --- ### Tips & Variations | Variation | How to Make It | |-----------|----------------| | **Honey‑Sweetened Sikhae** | Replace half the sugar with honey. Add a splash of vanilla extract for depth. | | **Fruit‑Flavored Sikhae** | Add ¼ cup of pureed fruit (strawberry, mango, or peach) to the batter before steaming. | | **Spiced Sikhae** | Stir in a pinch of cinnamon or nutmeg into the batter for a warm aroma. | | **Chewy Texture** | Increase the amount of glutinous rice flour slightly (up to 1 ¼ cups) and reduce water accordingly. | | **Mini‑Sikhae** | Pour the batter into small silicone molds or mini muffin tins for individual portions. | --- ### Storage - Store leftover sikhae in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. - For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 1 month). Reheat gently in a steamer or microwave (30‑60 seconds) before serving. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a delightful treat that showcases the simplicity and elegance of traditional Korean cooking.
